description: Veteran of 90 operational sorties with No. 460 Squadron RAAF. Returned to the Memorial on 31 July 2025 after five years in storage during the redevelopment and reassembled as the centrepiece of the Bomber Command display in the new Anzac Hall.
aliases: Lancaster; G for George; AR-G; Avro 683

description: Werknummer 500200. Surrendered German jet fighter-bomber shipped to Australia after the war. Last first-hand evidence is the Treloar Technology Centre "Big Things in Store" open day of September 2023 during the Memorial redevelopment; it may have returned to the galleries for the 2026 reopening.

Werknummer 191907, RAF Air Ministry number AM222. Rocket-powered interceptor. Last first-hand evidence is the Treloar Technology Centre "Big Things in Store" open day of September 2023 during the Memorial redevelopment; it may have returned to the galleries for the 2026 reopening.

Werknummer 163824, a G-6/AS. Last first-hand evidence is the Treloar Technology Centre "Big Things in Store" open day of September 2023 during the Memorial redevelopment; it may have returned to the galleries for the 2026 reopening.
Australian-built photo-reconnaissance Mosquito. ADF-Serials records it as on display at the Memorial in Canberra.

Korean War veteran of No. 77 Squadron RAAF that damaged a MiG-15 in combat. Formerly on static display at the Treloar Technology Centre; ADF-Serials records it as now on display in the Memorial Anzac Hall.
Afghanistan veteran flown to Canberra for the Memorial in April 2016 and stored at Treloar. Moved to the new Anzac Hall display on 4 September 2025 for the Kandahar Workhorse exhibit.
Retired 14 May 2020 with 6131.5 flight hours and transferred to the Memorial. The Memorial Anzac Hall gallery page describes an F/A-18A that served over Iraq and Syria as on display.
Painted and displayed as A2-1018, the RAAF Iroquois lost at Nui Dat in 1966. ADF-Serials records A2-389 on display at the Memorial.

The airframe used to validate the Bushranger gunship concept in Vietnam, later with 171 Squadron and flown to Christmas Island in 2001. Held at the Memorial aircraft storage and display hangar at Mitchell ACT for eventual restoration to Vietnam configuration.
Imperial Gift aircraft. Recorded at Treloar in September 2023 as A2-4; other surveys give the RAF identity D6950. The Memorial Aircraft Hall gallery page lists an S.E.5a on display.
Captured German scout and one of only two D.Va survivors worldwide. The Memorial Aircraft Hall gallery page lists it on display.

Captured German scout. Recorded at the Treloar Technology Centre in September 2023 as 2600/18; an earlier survey mislabels it a D.XIII 2600/13. Last first-hand evidence is the Treloar Technology Centre "Big Things in Store" open day of September 2023 during the Memorial redevelopment; it may have returned to the galleries for the 2026 reopening.

The Airco DH.9 flown from England to Australia in 1920 by Ray Parer and John McIntosh. Last first-hand evidence is the Treloar Technology Centre "Big Things in Store" open day of September 2023 during the Memorial redevelopment; it may have returned to the galleries for the 2026 reopening.
Early RAAF trainer listed in survey inventories of the Memorial display aircraft; its position after the redevelopment has not been re-confirmed.
The 1912 Deperdussin taxi-type single-seat trainer, described by the Memorial as the oldest existing Australian aircraft and listed on the Aircraft Hall gallery page.

Kittyhawk Mk.IA displayed as A29-133/S. Last first-hand evidence is the Treloar Technology Centre "Big Things in Store" open day of September 2023 during the Memorial redevelopment; it may have returned to the galleries for the 2026 reopening.
Listed among the Korean War aircraft on the Memorial Aircraft Hall gallery page.
Listed among the Korean War aircraft on the Memorial Aircraft Hall gallery page. Displayed as 109-K. Not to be confused with WG630 which is at HARS Albion Park.
Listed among the Korean War aircraft on the Memorial Aircraft Hall gallery page.
Listed in survey inventories of the Memorial display aircraft; its position after the redevelopment has not been re-confirmed.
Displayed as A20-103/D. Listed in survey inventories of the Memorial display aircraft; its position after the redevelopment has not been re-confirmed.

Australian-built Beaufort. Last first-hand evidence is the Treloar Technology Centre "Big Things in Store" open day of September 2023 during the Memorial redevelopment; it may have returned to the galleries for the 2026 reopening.
Japanese Army fighter, Allied reporting name Oscar. Listed in survey inventories of the Memorial display aircraft.

Ex-USAF forward air control aircraft of the type flown by RAAF FAC pilots in Vietnam. Last first-hand evidence is the Treloar Technology Centre "Big Things in Store" open day of September 2023 during the Memorial redevelopment; it may have returned to the galleries for the 2026 reopening.

Reconnaissance F-111C transferred to the Memorial; its forward fuselage donor FB-111A 68-0246 is at the Fleet Air Arm Museum. Last first-hand evidence is the Treloar Technology Centre "Big Things in Store" open day of September 2023 during the Memorial redevelopment; it may have returned to the galleries for the 2026 reopening.

Purchased by the Memorial in 2011 and returned to Australia from the United States. In storage at the Treloar Technology Centre. After service the airframe received a replacement rear fuselage, which has caused its identity to be questioned.

Ex-USAAF 43-49870. Last first-hand evidence is the Treloar Technology Centre "Big Things in Store" open day of September 2023 during the Memorial redevelopment; it may have returned to the galleries for the 2026 reopening.
Flight deck and nose section only, removed at RAAF Richmond for the Memorial; the remainder of the airframe was combined with A97-012 as a C-130J loadmaster training aid at Richmond.
Timor and Bougainville veteran that carried special tail markings in 2002 for 38 years of Caribou operations by 38 Squadron. ADF-Serials records it stored at the Memorial Mitchell annexe.
Held at the Museum of Australian Army Flying until 31 October 2000, then moved to Canberra and held in storage at the Treloar Technology Centre at Mitchell ACT.
Departed Edinburgh for the last time on 28 June 2018, stored at Avalon for the Memorial and transferred by road to the Treloar Centre / Mitchell annexe.
Served in East Timor with the United Nations in 2003; transferred to the Memorial in April 2019 for an East Timor display.
Royal Australian Navy Seahawk listed in survey inventories of the Memorial Mitchell storage holdings.
Royal Australian Navy Squirrel, coded 864 in Gulf service, listed in survey inventories of the Memorial Mitchell storage holdings.

Royal Australian Navy Wessex noted for the rescue of a fisherman from rocks near Point Perpendicular. Withdrawn 31 December 1989 to the Australian National Maritime Museum and transferred to the Memorial collection in 2019. Survey lists that give the Memorial Wessex as N7-226 are wrong; N7-226 is at the Fleet Air Arm Museum.
Listed in survey inventories of the Memorial Mitchell storage holdings.
Australian-built English Electric Canberra listed in survey inventories of the Memorial Mitchell storage holdings.
Vietnam veteran of 161 Recce Flight; then Army Captain J Campbell earned a DFC in this aircraft on 21 February 1967 after landing repeatedly in a minefield to rescue wounded soldiers.
Japanese Army twin-engined trainer recorded in survey inventories of the Memorial Mitchell storage. No manufacturer number has been published, so the tail number is left blank.
